Validation passes.

**Root cause:** `MessageDispatcher::route` was overloaded on `const Message&` vs `const PriorityMessage&`. Overload resolution in C++ is static (compile-time), based on the declared type of the reference/pointer, not the runtime type. The dispatcher call site (`test_001.cpp`) stores messages as `const Message*` in a heterogeneous vector, so `dispatcher.route(*msg)` always binds to `route(const Message&)` regardless of whether the pointed-to object is actually a `PriorityMessage`. That overload unconditionally enqueued to `standard_queue_`, ignoring `priority()` entirely — so HIGH/CRITICAL messages landed in the standard queue.

**Fix** (`src/dispatcher/message_dispatcher.cpp`): made `route(const Message&)` route by the message's actual `priority()` field — CRITICAL/HIGH → priority queue, LOW/NORMAL → standard queue, empty payload → DLQ — instead of relying on which overload got statically selected. `route(const PriorityMessage&)` now just delegates to the base overload, so behavior is consistent no matter which overload the compiler picks.

`validate_001.py` (compiles and runs `test_001.cpp`) now passes with `SUCCESS`.
